newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer despite LME stock hike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer despite LME stock hike.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer Thursday, shrugging off a weaker backwardation in London where LME stocks continued to rise sharply, two factors which usually put downward pressure on prices, dealers said.
"I think a lot of people are short and it has not been going down," John Tyree of FIMAT Futures said.
Shortcovering and borrowing on LME helped to push COMEX higher, along with some arbitrage buying, Tyree added.
LME stocks rose 13,025 tonnes Thursday to 173,350 tonnes, bringing the week's increase so far to more than 30,000 tonnes.
The bounce higher in modest turnover came despite the LME cash to three months backwardation weakening to $137/$147 Thursday, down from the $270 earlier in the week.
Dealers said they were waiting to see if there will be any follow through gains Friday to push LME three months, quoted late evening in London at $2,292/$2,294 a tonne, through the $2,300 level.
Some support was also gleaned from news that most miners at Portugal's Neves Corvo mine had rejected a renewed company offer.
